integrity: The claim follows from the exact series for \(k(d)\) in arXiv:2609.38450v1 by a positive-term monotonicity argument, dominated convergence, and an exact partial-fraction summation. Numerical decimals are illustrative only and are not used as proof.
limitations: The theorem concerns only the diagonal reaction-matrix example at the simple first transition and does not cover non-diagonal matrices or the higher-order case when the cubic transition number vanishes.
The exact closed form is for the large-d endpoint of the normalized coefficient, not for \(k(d)\) itself at arbitrary finite \(d\).

A public author research page mentions ongoing work on closed-form transition numbers but gives no public formula covering this coefficient; an equivalent unpublished derivation therefore remains a residual originality risk.
title: Sharp uniform envelope for the diagonal two-component transition coefficient
